classification.summary: For US customs, this is a travel bag (a weekender, heading 4202). Most of its outside (about 80%) is waxed cotton canvas and the rest is leather trim. A textile that has only been soaked in wax still counts as a textile, and the canvas is what gives the bag its main character. So customs should classify it as a travel bag with an outer surface of cotton textile that is not pile or tufted: 4202.92.15.00, at 6.3% (about $11.66 on a $185 value).

keyFacts.fact: The item is a 45-litre two-night travel bag (weekender) with a detachable shoulder strap. That makes it a 'traveling bag / travel bag' under heading 4202.
The body is 18 oz cotton canvas soaked in a paraffin-based wax. Leather (handles, base and trim) covers roughly 20% of the outside.
The main fabric is woven canvas, not a pile or tufted fabric. This matters because cotton pile or tufted bags fall in a 17.6% line.
The wax is paraffin with no plastic or polymer coating, so the outside counts as textile, not 'sheeting of plastics' (that line is 20%).
The canvas is all or mainly cotton by weight, with no significant synthetic blend.
Customs value is $185.00, quantity 1, country of origin United Kingdom (GB).
The brass hardware and cotton twill lining don't affect the code, because 4202 bags are classified by the material on the outer surface.

candidates.reasoning: Under GRI 1, the bag falls in heading 4202 as a traveling bag. Subheading 4202.92 covers bags whose outer surface is textile. Cotton canvas soaked in wax is still a textile material, and the subheading is decided by the outer surface. Here about 80% of that surface is waxed canvas, so the canvas gives the bag its essential character (GRI 3(b)) over the 20% leather trim. Under GRI 6, the line to use is 'Travel, sports and similar bags › With outer surface of textile materials › Of vegetable fibers and not of pile or tufted construction › Of cotton', at 6.3%.
candidates.decidingFact: The outer surface is mostly (about 80%) woven cotton canvas, which counts as a textile.

candidates.reasoning: If an officer decided the bridle leather handles, base and trim give the bag its character, the bag would fall under 'outer surface of leather › Other › Travel, sports and similar bags', at 4.5%. This is unlikely at about 20% leather coverage. It is also cheaper than the main line, so it doesn't raise the amount to hold.
candidates.decidingFact: Leather would have to cover most of the outside, or clearly be what makes the bag a bag. At about 20% it doesn't.

questionsForSeller: Is the wax only paraffin or another natural wax, with no plastic or polymer (for example PU or PVC) coating in the finish? If the fabric were plastic-coated, customs could treat it as 'sheeting of plastics' at 20%.
Is the canvas 100% cotton, or does it contain synthetic fibres? A canvas that is mainly synthetic by weight would be dutiable at 17.6%.
Can you confirm that leather covers only about 20% of the outside surface, and that the canvas body isn't covered or overlaid with leather anywhere else?
